gloss: to witness; to see (an event) happen

definitions.gloss: to witness; to see (an event) happen
definitions.explanation: To see something happen with one's own eyes, especially an incident, accident, or crime.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}を{目撃|もくげき}した。
{犯行|はんこう}の{瞬間|しゅんかん}を{目撃|もくげき}した{人|ひと}はいますか。
examples.english: Is there anyone who witnessed the moment of the crime?

examples.japanese: {通行人|つうこうにん}が{車|くるま}の{衝突|しょうとつ}を{目撃|もくげき}して、すぐに{警察|けいさつ}に{通報|つうほう}した。
examples.english: A passerby witnessed the car collision and immediately reported it to the police.

notes:
Literally "to strike the eye" — composed of {目|もく} (eye) + {撃|げき} (strike, hit). Used for personally seeing an incident, crime, or noteworthy event. Carries a stronger nuance than simply "seeing" — implies the event is significant or unexpected.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事故|じこ}を{目撃|もくげき}する: to witness an accident
- {犯行|はんこう}を{目撃|もくげき}する: to witness a crime
- {現場|げんば}を{目撃|もくげき}する: to witness the scene
- {目撃者|もくげきしゃ}: eyewitness
- {目撃|もくげき}{情報|じょうほう}: eyewitness information
- {目撃|もくげき}{証言|しょうげん}: eyewitness testimony

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見|み}る: to see, to look — general-purpose word with no connotation of incidents
- {目|ま}の{当|あ}たりにする: to witness firsthand — emphasizes emotional impact of seeing something up close
